newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen posting modest rebound.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen posting modest rebound.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to post a modest rebound on Friday, as stability in the yen is expected to aid a recovery in export-driven issues. Exporters' shares were pressured by heavy profit-taking during the yen's recent sharp rally, brokers said.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished 35.41 points or 0.18 percent higher at 19,877.39. Nikkei June futures rose 30 points to 19,850.
"Because of the stable currency market, major blue-chips are likely to cease falling," said Katsuhiko Kodama, general manager at Toyo Securities Co Ltd.
"The focus would be whether the Nikkei 225 closes above (the psychologically important level of) 20,000," said a senior broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
Brokers also said that weaker U.S. stocks overnight would be a negative factor, but the impact would be mostly offset by strength in the Nikkei futures overnight in Chicago.

On Thursday, the Dow industrial average closed 33 lower at 7258. In Chicago, the Nikkei June futures finished at 19,930, down 10 points from their previous close but up 80 points from Thursday's close in Osaka.
